title: UK CPI, February 2027 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the other print the 2027-04-29 MPC sees, and the last one whose reference month is wholly pre-lapse
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukfebruary2027, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads 'Consumer price inflation, UK: February 2027', 'Provisional release date: 24 March 2027 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published'. That is 07:00 London / 02:00 ET, a Wednesday. Filed estimate on ONS's own Provisional label, on this lane's no-self-confirm limit, and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2027-04-21
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-cpi-2027-04-21 LANE, 2026-09-09, because a claim two other lanes were carrying turns out to be a claim about TWO prints and the calendar knew only one of them. Both proposals for uk-cpi-2027-04-21 described the March 2027 print as 'the last hard inflation datapoint that committee gets' before the 2027-04-29 MPC + Monetary Policy Report. True of that print, misleading about the information set: this FEBRUARY print publishes 2027-03-24, SIX DAYS AFTER the 2027-03-18 MPC (BoE 2027 provisional dates, verified direct the same day and proposed separately as boe-decision-2027-03-18), so the 2027-04-29 committee receives TWO CPI prints since its previous meeting, not one. THE SECOND HALF OF THE INHERITED CLAIM SURVIVES AND GETS STRONGER: neither print can contain the SI 2026/987 electricity-VAT reversion, because February 2027's reference month is entirely pre-lapse and March 2027's ends on 31 March, the day before the zero rate expires (art. 1(2), read direct on legislation.gov.uk 2026-09-09: effect 'in relation to supplies made in the period beginning with 1st October 2026 and ending with 31st March 2027'). A committee that must publish a forecast embedding the reversion sees ZERO post-lapse observations across TWO prints. WHAT A RESEARCHER SHOULD NOT DO WITH THIS ENTRY: read it as another venue for the VAT step. It is not — it is a pre-lapse month with the drag flat inside it, and the electricity index does not move in February either (D7DT price-cap era 2019-2026: mean +0.011% m/m, largest 0.087%). Its value is as the second half of the April committee's information set, and as the last clean pre-lapse observation of a UK CPI print. Tiered low to match the whole uk-cpi series; symbols: [], no UK listing, gilt or sterling instrument on this calendar, and no rates- or FX-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
